en: Udāna 1.7 Ajakalāpakasutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Pāvā, at the Ajakalāpaka Shrine, in the abode of the yakkha Ajakalāpaka.
Now on that occasion, during the pitch-black darkness of night, the Blessed One was sitting out in the open air while a fine rain was falling drop by drop.
Then the yakkha Ajakalāpaka, wishing to arouse fear, trepidation, and horripilation in the Blessed One, [approached him].
He approached the Blessed One; having approached, he went three times near the Blessed One and made a confused noise, crying out "Akku-lo!
Pakku-lo!", saying: "This is a goblin for you, ascetic!"
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“When a brahmin has become one who has gone beyond regarding his own states, [he is truly a brahmin].”
Then one transcends both this Piśāca and Pakkula.
